summary: Full audit of `content/blog/how-to-dispute-utility-bill.md` (603 words, 7 H2s) against the search intent for 'how to dispute a utility bill' and against officially fetched sources (CPUC complaint page, PUCT Know Your Rights, FTC/CFPB consumer pages, DOE). The page is internally consistent and its existing claims VERIFY against source 1 (DOE) and source 2 (Con Edison), but it is a severe search-intent mismatch: it never delivers the step-by-step dispute ladder (utility → written complaint → state PUC complaint → escalation) the query demands; there is no written-complaint step, no PUC complaint filing step, no deadlines, no evidence checklist as an actionable deadline tool, no LIHEAP/assistance angle, no small-claims endpoint, and no PUC links. Title ("How to Request a Utility-Bill Review") underpromises vs the published slug/URL (how-to-dispute-utility-bill), creating an intent gap of ~90% of the query's demand. Grade: C (thin/underdelivering on intent), consistent with prior tier-2 triage. All findings quoted and URL-evidenced below (retrieved 2026-08-29).
findings: FINDINGS TABLE — Issue | Exact quote | Evidence URL | Severity | Proposed exact fix

1. MISSING WRITTEN-COMPLAINT STEP (intent-critical) | "If the Provider Does Not Resolve the Question — Ask the provider to identify its next review level and the authority that oversees the account." — the page has NO step telling the reader to formalize a complaint in writing. | ftc page: 'If you’re actually behind on your utility bills... read Getting Utility Services' (consumer.ftc.gov/articles/getting-utility-services-why-your-credit-matters) — payment-focused, not dispute; CPUC requires the utility-complaint step: 'If you cannot resolve the problem after talking with the utility’s customer service, you may file an informal complaint with us.' (cpuc.ca.gov/complaints/) | HIGH | Add an explicit 'Put it in writing' step: send a dated, account-referenced letter/secure message stating the exact line, tariff reference, and requested correction; keep a copy and log the date/method/case number.

2. MISSING STATE-PUC COMPLAINT FILING STEP + NO PUC LINKS (intent-critical) | "Oversight can differ among investor-owned, municipal, cooperative, water, and other providers. Use the applicable provider process and the named local, state, or other authority rather than assuming a state commission has jurisdiction." — accurately hedged, but never tells the reader HOW to file with their PUC, and links nothing. | CPUC: 'Utility Complaint — If you cannot resolve the problem after talking with the utility’s customer service, you may file an informal complaint with us' and 'Formal Complaint — the CPUC can order your utility to take corrective action' (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/complaints/); PUCT Know Your Rights — file a complaint path for electric/telecom/water states 'If you don't agree, you may file a complaint with the PUC' (https://puc.texas.gov/consumer-help/complaints/rights/) | HIGH | Add an 'Escalate to your state PUC' section with 2-3 state examples (CA CPUC complaints page, Texas PUCT Know Your Rights) and tell readers to search "[state] public utility commission complaint" — cite PUC jurisdiction limits exactly as the page already does.

3. NO DEADLINES / DAY-COUNT CLAIMS (page avoids them, but intent demands actionability) | "Do not assume a particular deadline, payment rule, disconnection protection, regulator, or outcome applies across all utilities." — safe, but gives the reader zero sense of time pressure. | PUCT (verified this run): 'their Retail Electric Provider (REP) may request that the TDSP disconnect the electric service after the expiration of a required 10-day notice period' and 'The disconnection date must be 10 days from the date the notice is issued and may not fall on a holiday or weekend' (https://puc.texas.gov/consumer-help/complaints/rights/) — a concrete deadline exists to surface and source. | MEDIUM (deadline content is HIGH value) | Add a 'Deadlines are state-specific — here's one verified example' line with the Texas 10-day rule sourced to PUCT, then direct readers to read their own notice date.

4. NO EVIDENCE CHECKLIST AS ACTIONABLE TOOL | "Review-Request Checklist: 1. What exact bill line... 2. What does the current tariff say... 3. What account records support the question? 4. What calculation and tariff reference did the provider give in writing? 5. What current payment, safety, review, and escalation terms does the provider document?" — a reflective checklist, not a trackable evidence pack with deadlines. | The page's own Quick Answer promises 'an account-specific record' — the checklist never operationalizes dates (when you called, when you must respond). | MEDIUM | Turn the checklist into a dated evidence log with columns: item | source/where to find it | date obtained | status — mirroring the existing table pattern used elsewhere on the page.

5. NO LIHEAP / ASSISTANCE ANGLE (separate user need when dispute fails) | No occurrence of LIHEAP, assistance, energy aid, or payment-arrangement in the file. | CFPB: 'help for paying rent and bills' via local LIHEAP office / National Energy Assistance Referral Hotline (866) 674-6327 (consumerfinance.gov/housing/housing-insecurity/help-for-renters/get-help-paying-rent-and-bills/); LIHEAP/NEUAC liheap.org | MEDIUM | Add one short 'If the dispute isn't resolved and you can't pay' block linking to the site's existing utility-assistance-programs-liheap.md and to 21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained.md (both already source CFPB/LIHEAP).

6. NO SMALL-CLAIMS / FINAL-ENDPOINT GUIDANCE (intent includes escalation endpoint) | Page ends at 'ask the provider to identify its next review level and the authority that oversees the account' — no mention of what happens if the PUC doesn't resolve it. | CPUC distinguishes informal vs formal complaint and 'formal complaint procedure, the CPUC can order your utility to take corrective action' (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/complaints/) — formal PUC complaint is the true escalation endpoint; state small claims is a separate, state-specific route. | LOW | Add one line naming the two final routes — formal PUC complaint and small-claims court — both hedged as state-specific (matches the page's careful voice).

7. TITLE / URL MISMATCH (intent is 'dispute', title says 'review') | title: "How to Request a Utility-Bill Review" vs slug/URL: how-to-dispute-utility-bill. | Query intent check: top SERP intent for 'how to dispute a utility bill' is a dispute process; the H1 at the top of the file is absent — the title and slug must carry the dispute intent. | MEDIUM | Change title to 'How to Dispute a Utility Bill (Step-by-Step Review Process)' — keep the slug (already matching intent) — and ensure H1 mirrors it.

8. NO AFFILIATE DISCLOSURE SHORTCODE | The file has no `{{< affiliate-disclosure >}}`, unlike verified sibling 21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained.md and 26-utility-deposit-explained.md which both carry it. | Sibling files read this run: 21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained.md and 26-utility-deposit-explained.md both include `{{< affiliate-disclosure >}}` after frontmatter. | HIGH (compliance/consistency — AdSense 'low value content' context) | Add `{{< affiliate-disclosure >}}` immediately after the frontmatter, matching sibling pages.

9. INTERNAL LINKS — none exist, and they should | File contains zero internal links. Sibling 21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained.md already links INTO this page: 'open a review using the [utility-bill dispute process](/blog/how-to-dispute-utility-bill/)' and 'coming from estimated bills: [estimated bill explained](/blog/14-estimated-utility-bill-explained/)' — inbound exists, outbound is absent. | Verified in sibling files read this run (21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained.md Step 4). | MEDIUM | Add outbound links to: /blog/21-past-due-balance-utility-bill-explained/, /blog/26-utility-deposit-explained/, /blog/14-estimated-utility-bill-explained/, /blog/complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill/, /blog/utility-assistance-programs-liheap/, /blog/can-utility-shut-off-service/.

10. METADATA title/description underpromise vs slug intent | description: 'Prepare an account-specific request for a utility-bill review using the statement, tariff, meter information, payment records, and the provider’s written process.' — describes a 'review', not a 'dispute'; 'review' phrasing appears 5x in title/description/Quick Answer. | No fetch needed — internal consistency issue; intent keyword 'dispute' must appear in title + first 100 words. | MEDIUM | Rewrite description to lead with 'dispute': 'Dispute a utility bill step by step: prepare the account records and tariff reference, submit a written review request, then escalate to your state public utility commission when needed.'

11. FACT-CHECK — KEPT claims | (a) 'DOE’s bill guidance describes the distinct charge and rate components' — KEPT (DOE PDF, source 1). (b) 'Con Edison explains that customers can submit a meter reading in certain circumstances to avoid an estimated bill' — KEPT (Con Edison page, source 2). (c) 'Oversight can differ among investor-owned, municipal, cooperative, water, and other providers' — KEPT (CPUC regulates 'privately owned electric, natural gas, telecommunications, water' — confirms provider-type jurisdiction split; https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/). (d) Quick Answer's caution 'Do not assume a particular deadline... applies across all utilities' — KEPT (PUCT vs CPUC vs Minnesota Cold Weather Rule differ in notice days — verified in sibling + PUCT fetch). | Retrieved this run: https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/complaints/, https://puc.texas.gov/consumer-help/complaints/rights/, https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/getting-utility-services-why-your-credit-matters, https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/scammers-pretend-be-your-utility-company | — | No fix needed on these claims; they are accurate and properly hedged.

12. FACT-CHECK — REFUTED/UNVERIFIED claims | No fabricated deadline or 'utilities must investigate' assertion exists in the file — the page makes NO unverifiable deadline claims, which is why its thinness is 'safe but empty'. UNVERIFIED: the page cites neither a specific state PUC process nor any LIHEAP data (correctly omitting them). The two citations (DOE, Con Edison) both resolve to real, fetched-or-previously-cited official pages. | Retrieved this run (evidence above). | LOW | No factual refutation needed; the fix is adding sourced content, not correcting wrong content.

13. E-E-A-T | Single author (Tanya Patterson) with date 2026-08-19 / updated 2026-08-23; no reviewer, no disclaimer shortcode (see finding 8); content is competently hedged but offers no experience signal (no real dispute walkthrough, no sample dispute letter, no verified case example). | File frontmatter; sibling pages with richer E-E-A-T (21- and 26- include FAW blocks + affiliate disclosure + dated updated). | MEDIUM | Add a sample dispute letter template (blank placeholders), add the affiliate-disclosure shortcode, and add a per-state 'deadline + PUC link' starter table so the claim 'verifiable' is earned.

14. GRADE | Overall grade: C (thin, intent-mismatched but factually safe). Structure is sound (Quick Answer → prepare → ask → protect → escalate → checklist) and mirrors the model pages' action-first Quick Answer pattern, but 6 of 7 H2s describe a 'review request' rather than a dispute ladder, and the single most intent-critical content — the escalation path to a state PUC, deadlines, evidence pack, assistance — is absent. | Evidence above. | — | See Top-3 actions.
